messages:
kevin: Quick trace heads-up — ran nsys on kv-prefetch branch against 8xA100 (NVLink enabled). Seeing repeated spikes in NVLink D2H/peer copies that line up with KV cache prefetch. TL;DR: peercopy kernels consume ~42% of timeline during long sequences, causing tail latency. nsys: https://perf.example/trace/1987 :eyes:

maya: link looks like peercopy bursts at model step 5-7, see kernel 'cudaMemcpyPeerAsync' and 'nv_peer_copy_v3' with long memcpy stalls. Can you paste the timeline range and a small perf summary?

kevin: pasted nsys summary:
```
Kernel timeline (sample):
- nv_peer_copy_v3: 42.1%  total  1.12s
- gpt_attn_forward: 18.3%  total  0.49s
- kv_prefetch: 12.4% total  0.33s
- cudaMemcpyAsync (H2D): 6.5% total 0.17s
```
Also NVLink bandwidth shows saturation ~78-85% during the peercopy windows.

liam: are pages pinned? pageable host memory forces staging copies H2D->pinned then H2D, which can blow up. Which allocator used by prefetch path?

kevin: currently using std::malloc + cudaMemcpyAsync. We didn't opt into pinned fallback. suspect the allocator mix is the issue.

sara: observed similar regression after the batching heuristic change (coalesce window reduced). If coalescing smaller, we issue more small peer copies which are inefficient. :thinking_face: 

dario: suggestion: 1) try cudaHostAlloc/pinned for prefetch buffers; 2) increase coalesce window to group adjacent cache keys; 3) switch kernel selection to copy_v2 (batched peercopy) when chunk_count > 8. Also add NVTX regions to demarcate prefetch vs kernel work.

kevin: running a quick pinned vs pageable experiment now. command I used:
```
nsys profile -o nvlink_case --capture-range=cpu_serialized ./inference_server --run-config=perf_small
# or nvprof --unified-memory-profiling off ./inference_server --trace-range start:end
```

infra-bot: scheduled perf run on 8xA100-nvlink cluster, job id perf-1987, ETA ~12m.

kevin: quick results (pinned vs pageable):
- pageable: peercopy kernel 1.12s, tail p99 latency 238ms
- pinned: peercopy kernel 0.34s, tail p99 112ms
Bandwidth differences align: pinned reduces staging, NVLink utilization steadier (less bursty).

maya: nice. We should make prefetch allocator default to pinned for Dedicated workloads, with opt-out flag. Also log when pageable allocations used so ops can detect it.

liam: also consider adding heuristic: if average key bytes > 64KB, prefer batched peercopy kernel; otherwise small-memcpy path for tiny keys. That should limit tiny-copy saturation.

sara: can we add a CI perf test that simulates fragmented prefetch (many small keys) and asserts peercopy kernel CPU time < threshold? attach nsight timeline snapshot to CI artifacts.

kevin: filed issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-3219 with traces and proposed patch. I'll prototype allocator switch and kernel selector.

dario: I'll review patch. Also add metrics: per-request NVLink bytes and peercopy kernel time to Console traces + rollout canary.

kevin: thanks — will follow up with PR + perf numbers. :thumbsup:
